questions.stem: Which opening suits a diary entry?
options: 'Sehr geehrtes Tagebuch,'
'Hallo zusammen,'
'Liebes Tagebuch,'
'Lieber Tagebuch,'
questions.explanation: 'Tagebuch' is neuter, so the informal greeting is 'Liebes'. 'Sehr geehrtes' is formal and would sound absurd to a diary, and 'Hallo zusammen' greets a group.

questions.stem: Which tenses best suit a diary entry written at the end of the day?
options: Mostly the perfect for the day's events, with the present for feelings now
Mostly the future, since a diary looks ahead to the next day
Only the present, because the entry is written on the same day as the events
Only the pluperfect, because all the day's events are over
questions.explanation: A diary entry looks back on what happened (perfect, with 'war' and 'hatte') and reflects on how the writer feels now (present). The future may appear for plans, but it does not carry the entry.

questions.stem: Which sentence best suits a diary entry?
options: 'Heute war echt ein komischer Tag, und ich weiß nicht, was ich davon halten soll.'
'Hiermit teile ich Ihnen mit, dass ich an dem Kurs im Mai leider nicht teilnehmen kann.'
'Laut Polizei wurde gestern Abend ein Radfahrer leicht verletzt.'
'Wir danken Ihnen für Ihren Einkauf und wünschen einen schönen Tag.'
questions.explanation: A diary is private and reflective, so a personal, informal voice about the writer's own feelings fits. The others belong to a formal letter, a news report and a shop notice.

questions.stem: How is the date usually written at the top of a German diary entry or letter?
options: 'Sydney, März 4.'
'Sydney, der 4 März'
'Sydney, am 4ten März'
'Sydney, den 4. März'
questions.explanation: German puts the day first as an ordinal number with a full stop, then the month: 'den 4. März'. The place often comes first, followed by a comma.

questions.stem: Which sentence is typical of a holiday postcard?
options: 'Bitte beachten Sie die neuen Öffnungszeiten.'
'Im Folgenden werden die Ergebnisse dargestellt.'
'Viele Grüße aus Salzburg! Das Wetter ist herrlich.'
'Hiermit bewerbe ich mich um die Stelle als Kellner.'
questions.explanation: A postcard sends brief, cheerful news from a place. The other sentences come from an application letter, a notice and a report.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of a postcard but not of a formal letter?
options: A subject line stating the purpose of the writing
'Mit freundlichen Grüßen' followed by a full name and signature
The formal 'Sie' and a list of enclosed documents
Brief news, a cheerful tone and a closing such as 'Bis bald!'
questions.explanation: Postcards are short and personal, written to friends or family with an informal greeting and closing. A subject line, 'Mit freundlichen Grüßen' and enclosures belong to formal letters.

questions.stem: Which closing suits a postcard to your grandmother?
options: 'Ganz liebe Grüße, deine Mia'
'Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Mia Schulz'
'Hochachtungsvoll, Mia Schulz'
'Sehr geehrte Frau Schulz'
questions.explanation: Family members are addressed informally, so a warm closing with 'deine' fits. The other closings are formal, and 'Sehr geehrte Frau Schulz' is a formal greeting, not a closing.

questions.stem: You leave a note on the fridge for your brother. Which suits?
options: 'Sehr geehrter Herr Bruder, ich teile Ihnen mit, dass ...'
'Gestern war ich beim Training und dann bin ich ...'
'Training ist wichtig für die Gesundheit junger Menschen.'
'Bin beim Training, komme um sechs. Pizza ist im Ofen!'
questions.explanation: A note is short and practical: where you are, when you will be back, what the reader needs to know. Formal address, a long recount or a general statement do not do that job.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of a short note ('Notiz')?
options: A headline followed by a subtitle
Dropped subjects, as in 'Bin gleich zurück'
A formal salutation and closing formula
Long subordinate clauses and the passive
questions.explanation: Notes are written in a hurry for someone you know, so 'ich' is often left out: 'Bin gleich zurück', 'Komme später'. Formal formulas and long clauses would be out of place.

questions.stem: You take a phone message for your host mother. Which version passes it on clearly?
options: 'Frau Becker hat angerufen. Sie kann morgen nicht kommen und ruft heute Abend zurück.'
'Ich bin Frau Becker. Ich kann morgen leider nicht kommen und rufe heute Abend zurück.'
'Hat angerufen. Morgen nicht. Zurück.'
'Frau Becker wird gestern anrufen, weil sie morgen nicht kommen konnte.'
questions.explanation: A message says who called, what they want and what happens next, written from the message taker's point of view. Writing as Frau Becker confuses the reader, and the clipped version leaves out who called.

questions.stem: Which message suits your teacher, Herr Klein, to say you are ill?
options: 'Lieber Klein, leider bin ich heute krank und komme nicht. Tschüss, Jonas'
'Sehr geehrter Herr Klein, leider bist du heute krank. Jonas'
'Sehr geehrter Herr Klein, leider bin ich heute krank. Viele Grüße, Jonas'
'Hi Herr Klein, bin krank, komme nicht. LG Jonas'
questions.explanation: A teacher is addressed formally with 'Sehr geehrter Herr' and his surname, and the message stays polite. 'Hi' and 'LG' suit friends, and 'Lieber Klein' without 'Herr' is rude.

questions.stem: Which information is essential in a notice ('Aushang') about a school event?
options: A story about last year's event
A dialogue between two speakers
What is happening, when and where
A personal greeting and closing
questions.explanation: A notice informs a general audience at a glance, so it needs a clear heading and the key facts: what, when, where and, if needed, who to contact.

questions.stem: Which sentence suits a notice on a school noticeboard?
options: 'Ich finde, Chorsingen ist das schönste Hobby der Welt.'
'Achtung: Der Chor probt ab Montag in Raum 12, nicht mehr in der Aula.'
'Lieber Max, wie geht es dir und deiner Familie in Wien?'
'Gestern ging ich nach der Schule in die Aula und hörte den Chor dort singen.'
questions.explanation: A notice gives readers practical information in a short, direct form. A personal letter, a recount and an opinion have different purposes.

questions.stem: Why do notices often use the infinitive, as in 'Bitte Tür schließen!'?
options: It is only correct in letters and emails
It gives a short, impersonal instruction to everyone
It shows that the event is in the past
It is the polite form for speaking to one friend
questions.explanation: An infinitive instruction avoids choosing between 'du', 'ihr' and 'Sie', so it addresses any reader. It is common on signs: 'Bitte nicht rauchen', 'Nicht hinauslehnen'.

questions.stem: Which details belong in a 'Gefunden!' notice?
options: A description of the finder's family and hobbies
The finder's opinion of the school's lost property rules
What was found, where and when, and how to contact the finder
Why the owner was careless and should be more careful
questions.explanation: The notice must let the owner recognise the item and get it back, so it gives the item, the place and time, and contact details. Opinions and personal background do not help.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a recount?
options: To describe a product for sale
To retell events in the order they happened
To persuade readers to take action on an issue
To give instructions for a task
questions.explanation: A recount retells an experience in time order, usually in the past tense, often with a personal comment at the end.

questions.stem: Which set of connectives best sequences the events in a recount?
options: 'jedoch, trotzdem, allerdings, dennoch'
'weil, denn, da, deshalb'
'einerseits, andererseits, außerdem, zudem'
'zuerst, dann, danach, schließlich'
questions.explanation: Time connectives move the reader from one event to the next. The other sets express contrast, cause and the weighing of arguments.

questions.stem: Which sentence makes the best opening for a recount?
options: 'Radtouren sind gesund und gut für die Umwelt, deshalb sollte man sie machen.'
'Morgen werde ich mit meinen Freunden eine Radtour an der Donau machen.'
'Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, ich möchte mich über eine Radtour beschweren.'
'Letzten Samstag haben meine Freunde und ich eine Radtour an der Donau gemacht.'
questions.explanation: A recount opens by setting the scene: who, when and where. The others open a persuasive text, a plan for the future and a letter of complaint.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct in a recount?
options: 'Am nächsten Morgen sind wir früh aufgestanden.'
'Am nächsten Morgen wir sind früh aufgestanden.'
'Am nächsten Morgen haben wir früh aufgestanden.'
'Am nächsten Morgen sind wir früh aufgestehen.'
questions.explanation: After a fronted time phrase the verb comes second, before the subject. 'Aufstehen' is a change of state and takes 'sein' in the perfect, and its participle is 'aufgestanden'.

questions.stem: Which sentence makes a good ending for a recount?
options: 'Dann haben wir am Bahnhof endlich unsere Fahrräder geholt.'
'Am Morgen hat es ein bisschen geregnet.'
'Es war ein anstrengender, aber unvergesslicher Tag.'
'Zuerst fuhren wir zum Bahnhof.'
questions.explanation: A recount often closes with the writer's reflection on the experience as a whole. The other sentences narrate single events from the beginning or middle.

questions.stem: Which features mark an article for a school magazine?
options: A greeting such as 'Lieber Max' and a closing such as 'Dein Tom'
The speaker's name in front of each line of the text
The place and date in the top right-hand corner
A headline, an engaging opening and paragraphs on one topic
questions.explanation: An article is written for many readers, so it needs a headline to draw them in and a clear structure. Greetings, speaker names and a dated heading belong to letters, scripts and diaries.

questions.stem: Which sentence suits a report on a school excursion rather than a diary entry?
options: 'Ehrlich gesagt fand ich den Bus viel lustiger als das ganze Museum.'
'Wer weiß, vielleicht werde ich eines Tages selbst Ingenieurin?'
'Am 12. Mai besuchten 25 Schülerinnen und Schüler das Deutsche Museum.'
'Ich war so aufgeregt, dass ich in der Nacht davor kaum schlafen konnte!'
questions.explanation: A report is factual and impersonal: date, numbers, place, written in the third person. Excitement, private jokes and personal hopes belong in a diary.

questions.stem: Which questions should a report answer?
options: Who, what, when, where, how and why
What the writer felt at each moment
Which arguments support the writer's view
What the reader should buy or do next
questions.explanation: A report gives the facts of an event, often checked against the 'W-Fragen': wer, was, wann, wo, wie, warum. Feelings and persuasion are not its purpose.

questions.stem: Which change makes a sentence in a report more objective?
options: 'Der Bürgermeister sprach' becomes 'Unser toller Bürgermeister sprach'
'Es kamen 200 Gäste' becomes 'Es kamen unglaublich viele Gäste!'
'Ich fand die Rede super' becomes 'Die Rede wurde mit viel Beifall aufgenommen'
'Die Rede dauerte 20 Minuten' becomes 'Die Rede war echt viel zu lang'
questions.explanation: Replacing a personal opinion with an observable fact, here in the passive, keeps a report objective. The other changes add opinion, praise or exaggeration.

questions.stem: How does the script of an interview usually begin?
options: With the interviewer's conclusion about the person
With the last question and its answer
With a short introduction of the person and the topic
With 'Liebes Tagebuch' and the date
questions.explanation: An interview script introduces the guest and why they are being interviewed, then sets out the questions and answers with the speakers' names or initials.

questions.stem: You are interviewing an Austrian skier you have never met. Which question suits?
options: 'Wie haben Sie dich auf die Saison vorbereitet?'
'Wie haben Sie sich auf die Saison vorbereitet?'
'Wie hast du dich auf die Saison vorbereitet?'
'Wie hat Sie sich auf die Saison vorbereitet?'
questions.explanation: An adult you do not know is addressed with 'Sie', which takes the plural verb 'haben' and the reflexive 'sich'. Mixing 'Sie' with 'dich', or using 'du', breaks the register.

questions.stem: Which line best closes the script of an interview?
options: 'Mit freundlichen Grüßen'
'Liebes Tagebuch, bis morgen!'
'Bis bald und liebe Grüße an deine Familie, deine Anna'
'Vielen Dank für das Gespräch und viel Erfolg!'
questions.explanation: The interviewer ends by thanking the guest, often with a good wish. The other lines close a formal letter, a diary entry and a personal letter.

questions.stem: The guest says 'Ich habe mit sechs angefangen, Geige zu spielen.' Which follow-up question best keeps the interview going?
options: 'Und was essen Sie eigentlich am liebsten zum Frühstück?'
'Was hat Sie damals an der Geige so fasziniert?'
'Spielen Sie eigentlich ein Instrument?'
'Haben Sie mit sechs Jahren angefangen?'
questions.explanation: An open question that builds on the answer invites the guest to say more. Asking what has just been answered, or jumping to an unrelated topic, breaks the flow.

questions.stem: Which sentence best ends the script of a talk?
options: 'Vielen Dank für Ihre Aufmerksamkeit.'
'Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Ihr Paul'
'Liebe Grüße und bis bald!'
'Betreff: Mein Vortrag'
questions.explanation: A talk ends by thanking the listeners for their attention. A letter closing and a subject line belong to written correspondence, not to a spoken text.

questions.stem: Which sentence helps listeners follow the structure of a talk?
options: 'Wir danken Ihnen für Ihren Einkauf.'
'Ich komme nun zu meinem zweiten Punkt.'
'Liebes Tagebuch, heute habe ich geredet.'
'Bin gleich zurück, warte auf mich!'
questions.explanation: Listeners cannot reread, so a talk signposts its structure aloud: 'Zuerst möchte ich ...', 'Ich komme nun zu ...', 'Zum Schluss ...'.

questions.stem: You give a talk to a group of Year 7 students. Which form of address fits?
options: 'du' and 'dich', since the speaker is only one person
'man' only, since direct address is not used in a talk
'ihr' and 'euch', since they are a group of younger students
'Sie' and 'Ihnen', since any audience of listeners is formal
questions.explanation: A group of children or teenagers is addressed with the informal plural 'ihr'. 'Sie' suits adults you do not know, and 'du' addresses one person.

questions.stem: In a letter to a friend, how may 'du' and 'dein' be written?
options: Always in upper case, and so must every other pronoun in the letter
Always in lower case, and so must the formal 'Sie' and 'Ihr'
In lower case in letters, but only in upper case in emails
Either way, but the formal 'Sie' and 'Ihr' always take a capital
questions.explanation: Since the spelling reform, 'du' and 'dein' are written in lower case, and in letters they may also be capitalised. The formal 'Sie', 'Ihnen' and 'Ihr' are always capitalised.

questions.stem: Which sentence keeps the right register in an email to the principal of your exchange school?
options: 'Könnten Sie mir bitte sagen, wann dein Unterricht beginnt?'
'Sag mir bitte schnell, wann der Unterricht beginnt.'
'Könnten Sie mir bitte mitteilen, wann der Unterricht beginnt?'
'Kannst du mir bitte sagen, wann der Unterricht beginnt?'
questions.explanation: A principal is addressed with 'Sie' throughout, and a subjunctive request is polite. Switching to 'dein' halfway or using the 'du' imperative mixes registers.

questions.stem: Which text type best suits this task: 'Tell all students that the library will close early on Friday'?
options: A recount
A postcard
A notice
A diary entry
questions.explanation: Short practical information for a whole group calls for a notice. A diary is private, a recount tells past events and a postcard goes to one person.

questions.stem: A task says: 'Your class went to a German film festival. Write about it for the school newsletter, giving your opinion of the films.' Which text type and register fit?
options: An article in a semi-formal register for students, parents and teachers
A diary entry in a private, informal register for the writer alone
A note in a clipped register for one friend who missed the outing
An interview script in a formal register with one film director
questions.explanation: A newsletter has a wide readership, so an article that informs and gives an opinion, in a clear semi-formal style, fits the purpose and audience.
